title: CEO 15s video captions + ops Q&A scratch
content:
Purpose: quick, human, and transparent 15s CEO video to (a) acknowledge slowdown in a region + temporary rate changes, (b) reassure customers/staff about fallback and cost controls, (c) point to support/exec Q&A. This doc is a scratchpad: captions, short script, and internal ops Q&A crib for on-call and comms folks.

Topline creative brief (why 15s):
- Social/portal embed: people expect short, visible update from founder.
- Tone: calm, direct, pragmatic. No techno-jargon. Humanize ops team.
- CTA: link to status page & 2pm all-hands Q&A.

Video structure (15s total)
- 0–2s: opener shot (CEO on camera) — friendly nod, headline caption: "Quick update from Redwood"
- 2–9s: one-sentence problem statement + what we did
- 9–13s: assurance + next step for customers
- 13–15s: CTA overlay + end

Suggested spoken script (very short) — CEO voice:
- "Hi — quick update. We saw constrained capacity in EU overnight; we routed most traffic and kept latency low, but a few customers hit limits. We're expanding capacity and will post an incident summary at 5pm. Thanks for your patience."

Captions (for feed – short, exact, 2 lines max):
Line1: "Quick update: limited capacity in EU overnight."
Line2: "We routed traffic, expanded capacity; incident summary @5pm."

Pinned hashtags (if posting externally/internal feed): #RedwoodStatus #InfraUpdate

Notes to producer/editor:
- Keep cuts tight; no B-roll. Use on-screen short captions matching the lines above.
- Add lower third: "Paulina Russo, CEO" (placeholder name for CEO).
- Ensure status URL visible as overlay in final 2s.

Ops Q&A crib (for internal staff/ops oncall + comms):
Q1: What happened?
A1: Brief: Overnight we had an unexpected increase in long-sequence generation jobs in eu-west-2 which exhausted reserved dedicated throughput for a small window (approx 22:10–22:25 UTC). Routing policies moved non-critical requests to burst pools; a handful of tenant-level rate limits applied.

Q2: Who was impacted?
A2: ~0.4% of hosted API requests in EU saw rate limit responses or slightly degraded latency; Dedicated customers with pinned capacity were unaffected unless they exceeded contracted throughput. We'll provide a customer list in the post-incident report.

Q3: Why did automatic fallback not absorb everything?
A3: Two factors: KV cache churn for long-context chats (reduced batching efficiency) + delayed autoscale due to node replacement times in zone during concurrent maintenance. We're changing autoscale thresholds and adding a short warm pool for long-seq workloads.

Q4: Is customer data at risk?
A4: No. This was an availability/performance event only. No integrity/authorization/exfiltration signals. Logs and audit trails unchanged.

Q5: What are immediate mitigations?
A5: 1) Temporary increase of burst capacity in eu-west-2 (done at 22:35 UTC). 2) Adjusted routing rules to favor lower-cost variants for low-priority traffic. 3) Short-term waiver for affected customers (credit) being drafted by CS.

Q6: Long-term fixes?
A6: 1) Add warm pool for long-sequence requests in each region. 2) Improve autoscale speed for replacement nodes. 3) Add proactive alerting on KV cache churn metrics. 4) Update runbook to automatically enable cross-region fallback for small tenants.

Internal talking points for 2pm all-hands Q&A (concise bullets for execs):
- What we know: small window of capacity constraint tied to long-context surge + maintenance overlap.
- What we did: prioritized traffic, increased burst capacity, routing fallback, CS outreach to affected customers.
- Impact: very small fraction of requests / no data breach.
- Next steps: detailed incident post-mortem by EOD + customer-facing summary at 17:00.

Notes-to-self / checklist before publish:
- [ ] Review CEO script with legal (check for absolutes like "no customers were affected") — be conservative.
- [ ] Ops to QA final numbers for "~0.4%" (if unsure, say "small fraction").
- [ ] CS to prepare templated outreach and credits policy.
- [ ] Product to prepare short FAQ for developer portal (3 Qs).
- [ ] PR/Marketing to prepare social copy variant for public posting (less internal detail).
- [ ] Tech lead to attach incident tracer links for postmortem.

Open questions / things to decide quickly:
- Do we publish CEO video internally only, or also to public channels? Suggest internal + status page + optional public trimmed version.
- Credit policy: automatic X credits vs case-by-case? Recommend small automatic credit for any tenant that received a 429.
- Should we call out specific services (embedding vs generation)? Probably avoid service-level naming in the quick video; use full details in postmortem.

Rough micro-timing for shoot (15 minutes total on set):
- 0–3m: run through script, pick final line
- 3–6m: 2 takes from camera A
- 6–9m: alternate framing for feed card crop
- 9–12m: export, captions embed, upload to internal drive
- 12–15m: ops + CS review + publish to internal feed

Last-line reminder: keep it human. No blame language. Focus on what we fixed and how customers can reach us.

Draft end-of-day postmortem outline (to be filled later):
- Timeline (minute granularity), root cause analysis, mitigation timeline, impacted customers list, monitoring gaps, action items owner'd with due dates.

-- ivy (scratchpad)
_comment: This file is a user scratchpad style doc for internal comms prep. Kept intentionally informal/fragmented per Google Drive usage rules.
